items.title: The Two Mindless Attainments: No-Perception and Cessation

items.zh: 無想定者，唯諸異生，由棄背想作意方便能入。滅盡定者，唯諸聖者，由止息想受作意方便能入。
items.en: The attainment of no-perception can only be entered by ordinary beings, by means of a mental engagement that turns away from and rejects perception itself. The attainment of cessation can only be entered by noble ones, by means of a mental engagement that brings perception and feeling themselves to rest.

items.zh: 如是二定，由二作意方便能入。謂無想定，由棄背想作意以為上首，勤修加行，漸次能入。若滅盡定，由從非想非非想處，欲求上進，暫時止息所緣作意以為上首，勤修加行，漸次能入。
若諸異生作如是念：諸想如病、諸想如癰、諸想如箭，唯有無想寂靜微妙。攝受如是背想作意，於所生起一切想中，精勤修習不念作意。由此修習為因緣故，加行道中是有心位，入定無間，心不復轉。如是出離想作意為先，已離遍淨貪，未離廣果貪，諸心心法滅，是名無想定。由是方便證得此定。
items.en: If some ordinary being reflects thus: all perception is like a disease, all perception is like a festering sore, all perception is like an arrow — only the absence of perception is peaceful and sublime … thus, with the mental engagement of stepping outside perception taken as the guide, having already left behind craving for the third dhyāna yet not yet left behind craving for the fourth dhyāna's great-fruit heaven, mind and mental factors cease — this is called the attainment of no-perception.

items.zh: 若諸聖者，已得非想非非想處，復欲暫時住寂靜住，從非有想非無想處心求上進；心上進時，求上所緣竟無所得；無所得故，滅而不轉。如是有學已離無所有處貪，或阿羅漢求暫住想作意為先，諸心心法滅，是名滅盡定。
items.en: If some noble one, having already attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, wishes to abide for a time in a still abiding, and seeks to advance further from that very mind of neither-having-nor-lacking perception; as the mind advances, the search for a further object yields absolutely nothing; and because nothing is gained, it ceases and no longer operates … thus, either a trainee who has already left behind craving for the sphere of nothingness, or an arhat, taking as guide the mental engagement of seeking a temporary abiding, brings mind and mental factors to cessation — this is called the attainment of cessation.

items.title: Section: The Five Superknowledges Open — Five Sources, One Genuine Path

items.zh: 復次，依止靜慮發五通等。云何能發？謂靜慮者，已得根本清淨靜慮。即以如是清淨靜慮為所依止，於五通增上正法，聽聞受持，令善究竟。謂於神境通、宿住通、天耳通、死生智通、心差別通等，作意思惟。
items.en: Furthermore, resting on dhyāna, one gives rise to the five superknowledges and the like. How does one give rise to them? One who cultivates dhyāna, having already attained the root, purified absorptions, takes exactly this purified dhyāna as the support, and, with respect to the excellent true teaching on the five superknowledges, listens, receives, and upholds it until thoroughly mastered — attending and reflecting upon the superknowledge of psychic power, of recollecting past abodes, of the heavenly ear, of knowing death and rebirth, and of discerning others' minds.

items.zh: 復由定地所起作意，了知於義、了知於法。由了知義、了知法故，如是如是修治其心。由此修習、多修習故，有時、有分發生修果五神通等。又即如是了知於義、了知於法，為欲引發諸神通等，修十二想。何等十二？一、輕舉想，二、柔軟想，三、空界想，四、身心符順想，五、勝解想，六、先所受行次第隨念想，七、種種品類集會音聲想，八、光明色相想，九、煩惱所作色變異想，十、解脫想，十一、勝處想，十二、遍處想。

items.title: Section: Psychic Power — Lightness, Softness, and a Mind the Body Simply Obeys

items.zh: 輕舉想者，謂由此想，於身發起輕舉勝解，如妬羅綿、或如疊絮、或似風輪。發起如是輕勝解已，由勝解作意，於彼彼處飄轉其身。謂從床上飄置几上，復從几上飄置床上；如是從床飄置草座，復從草座飄置於床。柔軟想者，謂由此想，於身發起柔軟勝解，或如綿囊、或如毛毳、或如熟練。此柔軟想，長養攝受前輕舉想。
items.en: The perception of lightness: by means of this perception, one gives rise, with respect to one's own body, to confident understanding of lightness — as light as cotton-down, or as a thick layer of fluffed cotton, or like a wheel of wind … the perception of softness: by means of this perception, one gives rise to confident understanding of softness — like a silk pouch, or the softest fur, or well-worked, refined silk floss. This perception of softness nurtures and sustains the preceding perception of lightness.

items.zh: 於攝受時，令輕舉想增長廣大。
空界想者，謂由此想，先於自身發起輕舉、柔軟二勝解已，隨所欲往，若於中間有諸色聚能為障礙，爾時便起勝解作意，於彼色中作空勝解，能無礙往。
items.en: The perception of space: by means of this perception, having first given rise, with respect to one's own body, to the two confident understandings of lightness and softness, then, wherever one wishes to go, if some mass of matter stands in the way as an obstruction, one gives rise to confident-understanding mental engagement, forming confident understanding of emptiness with respect to that very matter, and is able to pass through without obstruction.

items.zh: 身心符順想者，謂由此想，或以其心符順於身，或以其身符順於心。由此令身轉轉輕舉、轉轉柔軟、轉轉堪任、轉轉光潔，隨順於心、繫屬於心，依心而轉。勝解想者，謂由此想，遠作近解，近作遠解，麁作細解，細作麁解，地作水解，水作地解，如是一一差別大種展轉相作。
items.en: The perception of body and mind in mutual accord: by means of this perception, one either brings the mind into accord with the body, or brings the body into accord with the mind … the perception of confident understanding: by means of this perception, far becomes understood as near, near as far, coarse as fine, fine as coarse, earth as water, water as earth — thus each individual great element, one after another, is understood as transforming into another.

items.zh: 廣如變化所作勝解，或色變化、或聲變化。

blocks.text: Two attainments without mind, then the beginning of the five supernormal powers. A few short passages are untranslated.

"The attainment of non-perception can only be entered by ordinary beings, by an attention that turns away from perception. The attainment of cessation can only be entered by noble ones, by an attention that brings perception to rest."

An ordinary being reflects: "All perception is like a disease, like a festering sore, like an arrow; only the absence of perception is peaceful and sublime." Practising thus, they attain non-perception. A noble one, having reached the peak of existence, "wishes to abide for a time in a still abiding", seeks further, finds no object, and the mind ceases: the attainment of cessation (Day 147).

"Resting on purified absorption", having heard and upheld the teaching on the five powers (psychic power, recollection of past lives, the divine ear, knowledge of death and rebirth, and knowledge of others' minds), one cultivates a series of perceptions for each. Venerable Miào Jìng: the four absorptions of the form realm are the basis.

**Lightness**: understanding one's body "as light as cotton-down, or carded silk floss, or a wheel of wind". **Softness**: which "nurtures the perception of lightness". **Space**: when matter obstructs one's way, understanding it as space. **Mutual accord of body and mind**: the body follows the mind, the mind the body. **Confident understanding**: "far becomes understood as near, near as far".
The treatise treats psychic powers matter-of-factly, as a by-product of deep concentration. Its interest is not in wonders but in what they reveal about the mind's power over perception.

quiz.q: Why are non-perception and cessation together called "mindless attainments," according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "The attainment of no-perception can only be entered by ordinary beings … The attainment of cessation can only be entered by noble ones." Venerable Miào Jìng: non-perception and cessation both lack the sixth consciousness — hence "mindless attainments."

quiz.q: Noble ones enter cessation "wishing to abide for a time in stillness." What motive does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: not to eliminate perception and feeling, but to rest awhile
quiz.why: "Wishes to abide for a time in a still abiding, and seeks to advance further from that very mind." Master Cháng Bǎi: cessation isn't wanting to remove perception and feeling — it's wanting to rest for a while.

quiz.q: Ordinary beings in non-perception see "perception as disease, sore, arrow." How does Venerable Miào Jìng contrast them with Buddhists?
options: Buddhists have non-self wisdom; non-perception practitioners lack it
quiz.why: "If some ordinary being reflects thus: all perception is like a disease, like a festering sore, like an arrow — only the absence of perception is peaceful and sublime." Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddhist has the wisdom of non-self contemplation; one in non-perception lacks it — that's the difference.

quiz.q: Superknowledges rely on "attained, purified root dhyāna." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: powers mean the fourth dhyāna; claiming powers without it is a lie
quiz.why: "One who cultivates dhyāna, having already attained the root, purified absorptions, takes exactly this purified dhyāna as the support." Venerable Miào Jìng: if you have powers, you must have the form realm's fourth dhyāna; without it, claiming powers is lying.

quiz.q: Why must powers rely on root dhyāna? What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: desire-realm and access concentration can't — the dhyānas have calm and insight; Cháng Bǎi: the fourth balances them, the best support
quiz.why: "Takes exactly this purified dhyāna as the support." Venerable Miào Jìng: the form realm's four dhyānas are different — they have calm and insight, concentration and wisdom, so powers come easily. Master Cháng Bǎi: the fourth dhyāna is usually the best support, because calm and insight are balanced there.

quiz.q: Lightness "like 妒羅綿 or 疊絮" — rendered "cotton-down, carded silk floss." How do the lectures read them?
options: Miào Jìng: 妒羅 is a tree whose floss is very light; Cháng Bǎi, relaying Miào Jìng: wild silkworm cocoons
quiz.why: "Confident understanding of lightness — as light as cotton-down, or carded silk floss, or like a wheel of wind." Venerable Miào Jìng: 妒羅 is the name of a tree; the floss it produces is that light. Master Cháng Bǎi: imagining the body light as 妒羅綿 — Venerable Miào Jìng said it's wild silkworm cocoon. The two accounts differ.

quiz.q: "Softness nurtures and sustains lightness." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the two terms?
options: nurturing is growing from small to large; sustaining is not losing it once achieved
quiz.why: "This perception of softness nurtures and sustains the preceding perception of lightness." Venerable Miào Jìng: nurturing means from small to large, few to many; sustaining means not losing it once achieved.
